3

The image editor (imageeditor.html) edits raster images with layers: painting, shapes, text, gradients, selections, adjustments and filters, resizing, cropping, rotating, and the clipboard.

Files

Format Open Save
PNG, JPEG, WebP yes yes (JPEG and WebP with a quality setting)
BMP yes yes (24 bit)
GIF, ICO, SVG, AVIF yes (GIF: first frame; SVG is converted to pixels) –
OpenRaster (.ora) yes, with layers yes, with layers, opacity, blend modes and visibility
Photoshop (.psd) yes, with layers yes, with layers, opacity, blend modes and visibility

OpenRaster is the layered format of GIMP, Krita and MyPaint; Photoshop files are understood by most image programs as well. In PSD files, layer groups are opened as their single layers (hidden groups stay hidden), layer masks are applied to the layers, and text, shape and adjustment layers keep the pixels Photoshop stored for them (they cannot be edited as text or shapes). Saving in any other format merges the layers into one image; the application points this out. JPEG and BMP have no transparency; transparent areas become white.

  • File → New (Ctrl+N) asks for the size and the background (white, transparent or the background colour).
  • File → Open (Ctrl+O) opens an image; Open as layer adds images as new layers. Dropping image files onto the window opens them (or adds them as layers when you have already started working).
  • File → Save (Ctrl+S) and Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S, with format and quality): directly into the file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android.

Tools

Tool Key Use
✥ Move V moves the active layer; with a selection, the selected pixels
⬚ Rectangle selection, ◌ Ellipse selection M, Q drag to select (the size is shown while dragging); a click removes the selection; Shift for squares/circles; tool options: mode (free, fixed aspect ratio, fixed size – a click places it) and the position and size as numbers
➰ Lasso F drag around an area to select it freehand
⬠ Polygon lasso P click the corners; a double-click, Enter or a click on the first corner closes the shape, Backspace removes the last corner, Esc cancels
🪄 Magic wand W selects pixels of similar colour (tolerance; contiguous or all similar pixels of the layer)
🖌 Brush B soft-edged painting; the pen pressure of graphics tablets and styluses changes the size
✏ Pencil N hard pixels without smoothing (pixel art)
⌫ Eraser E makes pixels transparent
⎘ Clone stamp S Alt+click sets the source (on touch screens: ⊕ Set source, then tap), then paint: the pixels at the source are copied. Aligned: the source keeps its distance to the brush for every stroke; otherwise every stroke starts at the source. A cross shows the source
🩹 Healing brush J like the clone stamp, but the copied texture takes the colour and brightness of the place it is painted on – removes spots, scratches and blemishes without visible patches
👆 Smudge U drags colours along the stroke like a wet finger; the opacity sets the strength
◍ Blur / sharpen K paints a blurred or sharpened (mode) version of the layer; the size sets the radius, the opacity the strength
🪣 Fill G fills an area of similar colour (tolerance, contiguous or all similar pixels); right-click uses the background colour
▤ Gradient D drag: linear gradient from foreground to background colour
💧 Colour picker I takes the colour under the pointer as foreground colour (right-click or Alt: background colour)
╱ Line, ▭ Rectangle, ◯ Ellipse L, R, O drag; Shift for 45° lines, squares and circles; optionally filled with the background colour
T Text T click where the text should start; enter text, font, size, bold, italic
✋ Hand H or hold Space moves the view

The tool options (size, opacity, filling, tolerance) are on the right. [ and ] change the size, X swaps foreground and background colour. All painting tools work only inside the selection, if there is one.

Combining selections

With any selection tool, hold Shift to add to the existing selection and Alt to subtract from it; the tool option Selection (New, Add, Subtract, Intersect) does the same without keys, e.g. on a phone. Edit → Invert selection (Ctrl+Shift+I) selects everything else. Combined and magic-wand selections follow the pixels exactly; the move tool moves them like any selection.

Selections by coordinates

The status bar shows the position and size of the selection (⬚ x, y · width × height). With a selection tool, the tool options contain the fields X, Y, Width and Height: type values and press Enter (or Select) to select exactly that area. Edit → Selection by coordinates… does the same in a dialog (rectangle or ellipse), also on phones.

Rulers, guides and grid

Rulers along the top and left edge show image pixels and the pointer position (View → Rulers). Drag from a ruler into the image to create a guide (from the top ruler a horizontal one, from the left ruler a vertical one); with the move or hand tool, drag a guide to move it, or back onto a ruler (or out of the image) to remove it. View → New guide… places a guide at an exact position, Remove all guides removes them.

Snapping: selections, shapes, lines, gradients, text and moved selections stick to guides and – if switched on – to the image edges and the grid (View menu: Snap to guides, Grid, Snap to grid, Snap to image edges). View → Guides and grid… sets the grid spacing and how close the pointer must come (in screen pixels). Snapped edges lie exactly on the guide, so a selection between two guides covers exactly the pixels between them. These settings are remembered in the browser; guides belong to the open image and are not saved in the file.

Layers

The layer list on the right shows the layers from top to bottom. Click a layer to make it active; the checkbox shows or hides it, a double-click on the name renames it. Below the list: opacity and blend mode (multiply, screen, overlay, …) of the active layer, and buttons to add, duplicate, move up/down, merge down and delete layers. The Layer menu also flips a single layer.

Edit, image and filters

  • Edit: undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) up to 50 steps; cut, copy and paste (Ctrl+X/C/V, also with other programs through the system clipboard; pasted images become a new layer); select all (Ctrl+A), deselect (Ctrl+D), clear the selection (Del), fill the selection with the foreground colour.
  • Image: image size (with or without smoothing), canvas size (with anchor), crop to selection, rotate by 90° or 180°, flip, flatten.
  • Filters: brightness/contrast, hue/saturation (with live preview), levels, curves, auto levels, blur, sharpen, grayscale, sepia, invert, emboss, find edges. Filters change the active layer (inside the selection).

Levels… shows the histogram of the active layer (inside the selection) and sets the input black point, mid-tones (gamma) and white point, and the output range – for all colours (RGB) or for red, green or blue alone. Curves… maps brightness values with a curve: drag the points, click on the line to add one, double-click a point to remove it; an S-shaped curve increases the contrast. Both show the result on the image while the dialog is open; Reset restores the channel, Apply changes the layer (undo with Ctrl+Z).

View

Ctrl + mouse wheel or a pinch gesture on the touchpad zooms at the pointer, the mouse wheel scrolls. +, −, 0 (fit to window) and 1 (100 %) work as well; the buttons are at the bottom right. Zoomed in, pixels are shown sharply.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

On phones and tablets

The tools are in a bar below the image. Panels opens the tool options and layers. One finger paints, two fingers zoom and move the view. The menus can be scrolled sideways.
